statement: Adding an explicit temporal decay term to semantic retrieval is not novel in isolation: it is already instantiated as a lexical+dense+exponential-decay hybrid over a temporal benchmark and as learnable exponential decay inside graph-based retrieval. Therefore any contribution from the proposed idea cannot rest on the temporal-decay mechanism alone; it must rest on the retrieval-agnostic formulation, the amended-statute benchmark, and/or the distinction between recency and legal validity.

evidence.quote: We propose a three-signal hybrid framework integrating BM25 lexical matching, dense semantic embeddings, and exponential temporal decay, which achieves 99.8% temporal accuracy and 50.8% entity precision across all three languages
Layer 2 integrates learnable exponential decay functions into graph-based retrieval
